title: Visual Studio code injection permits network-triggered code execution
summary: Microsoft describes code injection in Visual Studio Tools for Applications and SQL Server Management Studio allowing an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network. The CVE lists affected Visual Studio 17.14 and 18.10 branches.

severity.rationale: The vendor vector requires user interaction but no attacker privileges. Developer workflows consuming untrusted content can meet this precondition; the primary record does not substantiate the lead's specific filename mechanism.

exposure: Requires the interaction described by the vendor vector. The cited CVE names SQL Server Management Studio but supplies no separate SSMS version range.

params.instructions: Read the installed Visual Studio branch and version. Check 17.14 against 17.14.42 and 18.10 against 18.10.4; obtain separate SSMS guidance from Microsoft.

remediation.details: Update affected Visual Studio branches to 17.14.42 or 18.10.4 or a later patched release on the same branch. Consult Microsoft for SSMS-specific updates.
remediation.risk: Low. Verify dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm the installed Visual Studio branch reports its patched release.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
